title: NLP: from Text Processing to Transformers
subtitle: Process, represent, classify and extract information from text in English, French and Arabic
audience_line: Data scientists and developers who work with text data
overview: This programme takes participants through natural language processing from classical text processing to Transformers and large language models. They clean and tokenise text, represent it with bag of words, TF-IDF and word embeddings, build classifiers for sentiment and other tasks, extract entities and relations, and discover topics. They then fine-tune BERT models with Hugging Face, handle multilingual text with attention to Arabic and French, and compare zero- and few-shot LLMs with fine-tuned models. Every chapter ends with a lab, and the programme closes with a final project: an NLP application on multilingual text built and presented by each team.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Data scientists and developers who work with text data

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Python and pandas (course: Python for Data Science) and deep learning basics (course: Machine Learning & Deep Learning, deep learning phase), or equivalent. These are used, not taught

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 27 h: 24 h of chapters + 3 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs in Jupyter on English, French and Arabic corpora

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant (16 GB RAM, Python 3, JupyterLab, spaCy, NLTK, Hugging Face); GPU notebooks on Google Colab or a GPU server provided by the organiser for fine-tuning; an open LLM through Ollama or on the GPU server, or a hosted LLM API key per team with a spending cap, provided by the organiser

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can build, fine-tune and evaluate NLP models for classification and extraction on English, French and Arabic text, and judge when an LLM is the better tool

phases.name: Text Processing & Representation
phases.focus: NLP tasks, tokenisation, normalisation, bag of words, TF-IDF, word embeddings
phases.intro: Participants see what NLP is used for, then turn raw text into clean tokens with spaCy, NLTK and regular expressions, and into numbers with bag of words, TF-IDF, word2vec and GloVe. Validated lab: a preprocessing pipeline for French and English reviews, and the nearest neighbours of chosen words in an embedding space.

chapters.title: Introduction & Text Processing
chapters.content: Tasks and applications, tokenisation, normalisation, stemming and lemmatisation, regular expressions, spaCy and NLTK

chapters.title: Text Representation
chapters.content: Bag of words, TF-IDF, word2vec, GloVe

phases.name: Classical NLP Tasks
phases.focus: Classification and sentiment, named entities and relations, topic modelling
phases.intro: Participants build classical and neural classifiers for sentiment and other labels, extract named entities and relations, and discover the topics of a corpus with LDA and BERTopic. Validated lab: a sentiment classifier evaluated on a held-out set, and the main topics of a news corpus found with LDA.

chapters.title: Topic Modelling
chapters.content: LDA; BERTopic as a preview of Transformer embeddings

phases.name: Transformers & LLMs
phases.focus: BERT fine-tuning, multilingual NLP, LLMs for NLP tasks
phases.intro: Participants fine-tune BERT-family models with Hugging Face, handle translation and the specifics of Arabic and French text, then use LLMs for zero- and few-shot classification and extraction and compare them with the fine-tuned models. Validated lab: the same classification task solved by a fine-tuned multilingual model and by an LLM, with accuracy and cost compared.

chapters.title: LLMs for NLP Tasks
chapters.content: Zero- and few-shot classification and extraction, evaluation against fine-tuned models

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A multilingual NLP application, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three build an NLP application for classification or extraction on Arabic, French or English text, reusing the phase labs, then present it as they would to a product team.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, prepare the corpus, build a baseline and fine-tune a Transformer model

chapters.title: Evaluate & Document
chapters.content: Evaluation per language, error analysis, comparison with an LLM, short report

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo on new text; questions and feedback

project.title: A Multilingual NLP Application
project.brief: An application that classifies text or extracts information from Arabic, French or English documents with a fine-tuned Transformer model, evaluated per language and compared with a baseline and an LLM.
project.stack: Python, spaCy, Hugging Face Transformers and Datasets, scikit-learn, PyTorch, JupyterLab
project.deliverable: Repository with notebooks and model, evaluation report, live demo
